key_provisions_or_claims: Public trust in humanoid robots depends on emotional, symbolic and cultural factors, not only technical performance.
Ethical principles like transparency and fairness are interpreted through local social contexts.
Introduces the Human–Robot Integration Ethics Matrix (HR-IEM) linking algorithmic objectives to social trust indicators.
Identifies overreliance on lab studies and lack of participatory, cross-cultural design.
Advocates adaptive ethics modules, participatory feedback and co-design.
annotation.summary_en: Qualitative interdisciplinary narrative review on public trust and ethical algorithm design in humanoid robots. Proposes the Human–Robot Integration Ethics Matrix (HR-IEM) linking ethical objectives to social trust indicators, and calls for adaptive, participatory, culturally sensitive ethics design for responsible societal integration.
annotation.title_clean: Humanoid Robots, Public Trust, and Ethical Algorithm Design: A Multidisciplinary Framework for Societal Integration and Future Adoption
annotation.title_en: Humanoid Robots, Public Trust, and Ethical Algorithm Design: A Multidisciplinary Framework for Societal Integration and Future Adoption
annotation.venue: Journal of Computational Systems and Applications
